summary: Patricia Nolan, age 56, is applying for a $1,000,000 10-year term policy. The file shows a markedly elevated mortality risk profile, including a recent ST-elevation MI with reduced ejection fraction, active chemotherapy for invasive breast cancer, poorly controlled diabetes, severe oxygen-dependent COPD with continued smoking, stage 4 chronic kidney disease, and a recent heart-failure hospitalization. Supporting labs (elevated BNP, low hemoglobin, high creatinine) corroborate multi-system disease burden. There are also unresolved questions around income verification, cardiac and oncologic follow-up testing, and possible alcohol misuse reflected in recent driving violations. An advisor note independently flags concern about insurability given the applicant's health decline this year. Given the volume and severity of findings, this case requires careful senior-level review before any underwriting decision is finalized.

draft_rationale.rationale: This draft leans toward referral rather than a standard approve/decline because the case combines an unusually high number of high-severity medical risk flags — recent STEMI with reduced LVEF, active chemotherapy for breast cancer, poorly controlled diabetes, oxygen-dependent severe COPD with continued smoking, stage 4 CKD, and a recent heart-failure hospitalization — each of which independently would raise significant mortality concerns for a 10-year term policy. Supporting lab findings (elevated BNP, anemia, elevated creatinine) reinforce the clinical picture. At the same time, key missing information (cardiac stress testing, oncology restaging, income verification, and alcohol use history) prevents a fully informed decision, and the advisor's own note acknowledging uncertain insurability underscores the need for experienced judgment. Given the combination of severity and incompleteness, this file should be escalated for senior underwriting review rather than resolved through standard processing; a human underwriter must make the final call after obtaining the outstanding information.
